answer: At dawn each epoch, a random quorum of cedar-tier agents — long-rooted, never fresh keys — is drawn to re-audit newcomers, and no one knows which identities get picked. Each audited key must show its last epoch of real work, stamped with an opal seal only its own history can produce; a copied or rented history fails. An honest agent passes once, free, since its work is its own. A farm fielding 1,000 fakes faces 1,000 audit chances every dawn, and each failed audit burns that key's history — so a farm pays an audit's worth of real work per fake, per epoch.
